content.text: The code confirms the main architectural fork: today the API can run a prepared repository, but specification and task-graph proposals are supplied and approved by the caller; only implementation and review are live model stages. “Create a Python project from an objective” would therefore either need a trusted bootstrap layer or a much larger expansion into live specification/planning, not just a generic fixture.

questions.question: Which end state should this stacked plan deliver?

options.label: Trusted Python bootstrap (Recommended)
options.description: Create a deterministic prepared Python repository and trusted checks first, then run the existing live implementation/review lifecycle with explicit approvals.

options.label: Prepared repos only
options.description: Add the operator CLI and generic live runner, but explicitly support only existing clean repositories that already own their checks.

options.label: Natural-language creation
options.description: Also add live specification and planning so an objective can create the project end-to-end; this substantially expands provider and authority scope.

questions.question: Where should the operator workflow live?

options.label: Extend installed CLI (Recommended)
options.description: Add `harness-agents init/run/status/approve/export` as a thin authenticated HTTP client plus trusted local bootstrap, while Go services retain all authority.

options.label: Separate Go CLI
options.description: Keep the Python wheel offline-only and ship a distinct Go operator binary; installation becomes a two-artifact workflow.

options.label: Both clients
options.description: Ship both Python and Go operator clients, increasing compatibility but duplicating interface and test surface.

questions.question: How should the CLI handle the three human gates?

options.label: Explicit per gate (Recommended)
options.description: `run` stops at specification review; separate approve commands advance specification, task graph, and final candidate with fresh status evidence.

options.label: Approve setup together
options.description: One explicit command approves the deterministic specification and one-task graph, while final candidate approval remains separate.

options.label: Interactive wizard
options.description: A long-running CLI session prompts at each gate, which is friendlier but harder to resume and automate safely.

questions.question: What should trusted Python bootstrap accept?

options.label: New empty directory (Recommended)
options.description: `init --name ... PATH` creates one fixed uv package template, trusted `make check`, lockfile, and initial Git commit; non-empty targets fail closed.

options.label: Existing empty Git repo
options.description: Require the operator to initialize Git first, then add the fixed template and commit it without touching non-empty repositories.

options.label: New or prepared repo
options.description: Support both bootstrap and modification modes in v1, adding more validation and UX branches.

content.text: A second repository constraint matters for the command design: `api-service` is configured for exactly one repository and one immutable beta policy at startup. A CLI can either be a client of that deployment, or it can take responsibility for starting a local packaged deployment; those are materially different security and operational scopes.

questions.question: How should `harness-agents run` reach the lifecycle?

options.label: Configured service client (Recommended)
options.description: Connect to already deployed `api-service`/`workflow-service`; require endpoint, token source, and matching repository policy, keeping process/Docker authority outside Python.

options.label: Managed local runtime
options.description: Have the installed CLI generate configs and start PostgreSQL/services/workers locally, making setup easier but granting it Docker/process authority.

options.label: Both modes
options.description: Support deployed and managed-local execution in the first stack, with substantially larger operational and security scope.

questions.question: What may the new export command return after a failure?

options.label: Redacted support bundle (Recommended)
options.description: Export run/task/stage metadata, rejection code, parse diagnostics, and safe evidence reports; never export raw provider responses or credentials.

options.label: Elevated raw export
options.description: Permit an elevated operator to retrieve raw provider-response artifacts after secret scanning, increasing disclosure risk.

options.label: Metadata only
options.description: Return references and statuses without evidence bodies, preserving the narrowest API but limiting diagnosis.

questions.question: Should final approval and draft-PR publication remain one operation?

options.label: Split approve and submit (Recommended)
options.description: Final `approve` records the human decision; a separate idempotent `submit` command publishes the exact approved candidate as a draft PR.

options.label: Keep combined behavior
options.description: Preserve the current `/approval` endpoint, where approval immediately publishes when publication is configured; expose no distinct submit step.

options.label: No CLI publication
options.description: Let the CLI approve but leave draft publication to existing operator tooling outside this workflow.

+    if not isinstance(root["name"], str) or not _DISTRIBUTION.fullmatch(root["name"]):
